agreed.amal_said: No. You're a key. You can't open.
agreed.why: He reached for 'relaxed' and said مفتوح / مفتاح (open / key); Amal said No, you're a key, and he then found مرتاح (her chat ana mertaa7).

agreed.medi_said: اشتغلت، اه بيتي. من بيتي؟ لا، اشتغلت بيتي.
agreed.why: He floated من بيتي then rejected it ('لا، اشتغلت بيتي'); Amal said Yes, صح، من بيتي - the preposition min is needed.

agreed.medi_said: الأخيرة. / It's right. اجتماعات الأخيرة، right?
agreed.amal_said: No، اجتماع is masculine. ... You don't need a t.
agreed.why: He put the feminine adjective الأخيرة on اجتماع; Amal said No, اجتماع is masculine, you don't need a t, and he then said اجتماعي الأخير.
Clock time needs el-: he said على واحد / واحدة, Amal recast الوحدة and he repeated الواحدة (her chat 3ala el-wa7de).

agreed.chat: shu el-yoam yoam el-5amees, 5amse e7da3sh alfain u sitte u 3eshreen
agreed.why: In a date the number stands alone and keeps its -e (5amse); Amal said No, he fixed to خمسة, and she then asked when the number drops its ending (only when counting a noun).
Clock time takes the feminine number (tentain); he said اثنين, Amal let it pass in voice and only typed tentain illa tult (chat alone is not a correction, GR-19).
Same rule as 06:25: a bare number keeps its -e (5amse u sitteen); Amal said No, مش خمس.

agreed.amal_said: That's I don't miss. I don't complain.
agreed.why: Asked for 'I don't complain' he said بشتاقش (I don't miss), a different verb; Amal said that's I don't miss and he switched to بشكيش (sheet: complain | Eshki | اشتكي).

agreed.amal_said: مهم. Where's the t؟ You keep the t.
agreed.chat: ma / tenze3jesh min ay ishi taani
agreed.why: A negative command is built on the you-form with its t- prefix; he said زعجش with no t, Amal said Where's the t? You keep the t.

agreed.chat: ma / tenze3jesh min ay ishi taani
agreed.why: After her t fix he dropped the t- again (انزعجش, past/command stem); Amal said la, it doesn't work, تنزعجش - its own slip after the fix (GR-32).

agreed.amal_said: About anything else. ... هيك issue something like this.
agreed.chat: ma / tenze3jesh min ay ishi taani
agreed.right: من إشي ثاني (min ay ishi taani)
agreed.why: For 'about anything else' he said min heik (from this / like this); Amal repeated 'About anything else' twice and said heik is 'something like this', then he said من إشي ثاني.
He asked how to say 'too much'; Amal pointed him to 'Extra' (sheet: extra / increase | Ziaadeh | زيادة), which he then used.
Negative verb needs the -ish ending after ma; Amal asks 'Where's your ish?'
agreed.proposed_rule: With ma + a present/command verb add the -ish ending: ma tinbastish (Amal: Where's your ish?)

agreed.why: He said زياد (a man's name) for زيادة; Amal echoed 'Zia' and he completed زيـ زيادة - may just be a cut-off word (S5).

r1.chat: ijtimaa3i el-a5eer / aa5er ijtimaa3 ili kaan 3ala el-wa7de
r1.why: For 'my last meeting' he put aa5er on a plural with a possessive ending (= the last of my meetings / end of); Amal prompted ('Did you add in?', 'It's one. اجتماع.') and typed aa5er ijtimaa3 / ijtimaa3i el-a5eer.

r2.chat: ijtimaa3i el-a5eer / aa5er ijtimaa3 ili kaan 3ala el-wa7de
r2.why: 'last meeting' needs aa5er + singular noun; Amal: 'It's one. اجتماع.' and 'Plural.' after he asked about the plural.

r1.why: He understood her هذي الفترة as 'at this moment'; Amal said No and repeated it, and he then worked out فترة = this period of time.

After the Arabic number failed he said English 'sixteen' (sheet: 'sixteen | sitta3sh | ستاعش', 'sixty | sittin | ستين'); her chat shows he meant 65 - pre-ruled tier-3 let-pass (AR-1933); may be the engine for 'sixty-'.

r1.medi_said: Is it بعيد؟ بعيد becomes bad?
r1.why: He heard her بدت and guessed it came from بعيد (far); Amal said no, it is from بدا (started).

r2.medi_said: Is it بعيد؟ بعيد becomes bad?
r2.why: He guessed the word she said (بدت) was بعيد; she says no, it comes from بدأ.

r1.chat: ma / tenze3jesh min ay ishi taani
r1.why: He used the za3aj (annoy someone) stem instead of the n- form inza3aj (get annoyed); Amal said Again, he reached بنزعج, she confirmed 'بنزعج، صح' and he noted 'There's an N'.
Same t- drop she fixed at 23:04 and 23:40 (negative command needs the you-form t-); here she let it pass in voice and only typed tenbestish.

r2.why: Plural of آخر: she lists آخرات then أواخر (أها); his أخيرات looks like an invented plural pattern.

r2.medi_said: for بارد I can use like باردات؟
r2.why: He asked whether the plural adjective باردات works; Amal 'No' and shows the singular feminine. It is a rule question, so low.
Non-human plural takes the feminine singular adjective; he added plural -aat and Amal: 'No. صعبة.'

r2.medi_said: Oh yeah, فيه. ما تنبسطي فيه
r2.why: He dropped the -ish again after her first prompt; she asked 'Where's your ish?' a second time.
r2.proposed_rule: With ma + a present/command verb add the -ish ending: ma tinbastish (Amal: Where's your ish?)

r2.amal_said: بحكيش. See these verbs that end with a long vowel؟ We keep them long
r2.why: Attempting 'I don't speak' with -sh he gave behkesh/behkish; Amal states that verbs ending in a long vowel keep it long.
r2.proposed_rule: Verbs ending in a long vowel keep it long before -ish: بحكيش, بمشيش
